experiment.claim: README.md 'Target specification (ratified -- see DR-005, issue #1)' row 'Startup time' (< 1 ms), for the 3.3 V primary flavor (DR-001). Ramps the supply feeding the ROUTED bandgap-core layout (issue #62, thick-oxide geometry per issue #620; its LVS verdict is cited under 'Netlist provenance', not asserted here) from 0 V to the corner supply in t_ramp and measures the first time VREF rises through 1.08 V (90% of the 1.20 V draft nominal), open-circuit, over the full 45-point PVT matrix, via klt extract --parasitics translated to a simulatable netlist (sim/bin/post_layout_common.py) -- NOT design/bandgap_core.sch directly; see 'Netlist provenance' below. NOTE: the no-injector caveat the schematic-level manifest carries does NOT apply to this record any more (issue #285). The composed cell now DRAWS design/startup_injector.sch -- six devices (MPC1, MPC2, MNS, MNI, MNC, QS), LVS-matched against a reference netlist that carries them too -- so this bench measures the extracted core AS DRAWN, injector included, while the wrapped schematic bench stays the bare core. The two halves of this spec line therefore measure DIFFERENT circuits on purpose: schematic = the unprotected core (parks in the all-off degenerate state), post-layout = the cell that would be fabricated. Read this record against the layout record named under 'Netlist provenance', not against the schematic-level record.

experiment.title: Supply-ramp startup time of the untrimmed core over the full PVT matrix -- POST-LAYOUT (extracted netlist)

spread_checks.note: The settled supply must move by at least 0.5 V across the matrix (2.97 -> 3.63 V is 0.66 V). This is the corner-liveness check for this bench: it proves the runner's supply knob reaches the simulator. It is deliberately NOT placed on t_start_ms or vref_final -- if the core does not self-start, those are pinned at their sentinel/zero values by the physics under test, and a spread check on them would report a second, redundant failure that says nothing new.
